newsitem.title: UK: UK companies contract out more in 1990s - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK companies contract out more in 1990s - survey.

text.p: British firms have increased the amount of work they contract out by 66 billion stg since 1989, a report out on Monday showed.

The report, by the Foundation for Manufacturing and Industry and the Chartered Institute for Purchasing and Supply, highlights the growing trend for companies to focus on core activities and outsource other work to outside contractors.
The report said information technology, catering, cleaning and financial services firms are prime beneficiaries of the trend to contract out.
"This has accounted for some, but not all, of the reduction in the numbers of people employed in manufacturing and the increased in the numbers in services," the report said.
The biggest gainers from contracting out between 1979 and 1994 were road and inland transport services, office machinery and computer equipment, postal services and telecommunications.
"New companies are springing up ready to offer package deals to firms anxious to contract out part of their activities," said Douglas McWilliams, chairman of the FM&I's research committee.
"Outsourcing has become a new growth industry in which Britain is leading the world."
